newsitem.title: USA: Kennedy wants healing after brother's case dropped.
newsitem.headline: Kennedy wants healing after brother's case dropped.

text.p: Representative Joseph Kennedy said on Wednesday he hoped for "healing" after a prosecutor decided not to file charges against Kennedy's brother Michael over allegations he had sex with the family's teenage babysitter.
"Obviously this is a time when I hope that there can be healing in Michael's family," Kennedy told reporters. Both men are sons of the late Sen. Robert Kennedy.

"There can only be a sense of pain that has come out of all these circumstances and I'm sure that he and Vicky and their children ... all find a way to put these very, very tough and difficult times in the past," said the Massachusetts Democrat.

The alleged affair, first printed in the Boston Globe in late April, became public shortly after Michael Kennedy separated from his wife Victoria Gifford Kennedy, the daughter of sportscaster Frank Gifford.

Asked whether he still planned to run for Massachusetts governor in 1998, Joseph Kennedy replied, "Yes, I fully intend at an appropriate time to get involved in that campaign, but at an appropriate time."
In Massachusetts, Norfolk County District Attorney Jeffrey Locke said on Tuesday he would not file charges against Michael Kennedy because the alleged victim would not cooperate.

Locke began his investigation after the Globe reported that Michael Kennedy, 39, head of the nonprofit Citizens Energy Corp., had a five-year affair with the babysitter that started when she was younger than 16. Now 19 and a Boston University student, the woman turned 16 at the end of January 1994.
